title: Records and radio; first seeing Ellington at the Apollo with his parents
summary: He learned from radio and a few records, especially Ellington, and remembers his parents taking him to the Apollo where he focused on the bass player.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What kind of -- did you all have any -- any particular bands that you were emulating at that time. Who were they -- you know, what records -- were you all listening to records, modeling what you were doing off -- from records that were around, from radio broadcasts, or did Marshall himself have

own
records on book?
No, listening to radio and a couple of records that my folks had gotten for me, you know.
Do you remember whose recordings you listened to?

Yeah. Duke Ellington especially. And I remember first time that I saw Duke Ellington and his band in person, my folks took me over to the Apollo Theater at 125th Street in New York to see him. He was appearing there.
How old were you then, about?
I was around, oh, 19, somewhere.
So this was near 1930? You were born in 1914 --
Yes.
-- no, that would be somewhere after --
About '33, something like that.
Who was playing bass with the band?
Oh, gee -- what was his name?
Wellman Braud, was it Wellman Braud?
No. Braud wasn't -- the name was Green -- Greenstreet -- Green -- I forget his name. I don't think Wellman Braud was playing with him. "Bro," I think how you think how you propounce that.
You know, Sonny Greer says "Bro," so maybe that's what it was.
Braud, Wellman, yes.
Maybe it was --
It may have been Wellman Braud. But anyway, I will never forget that first visit, you know, the folks taking me over to see the band at the Apollo.
And so like what kind -- do you remember . So you were really impressed by the band.
Yes, I was.
Could you hear the bass well?
Yes, I did.
Now, were they --
That was my main -- my main interest there, the bass fiddler.
Uh-huh. Was -- at that time was the bass -- did they use amplification for the bass of any sort, the bass player?

No, they probably had mikes -- a mike nearby so he could be heard. I heard the whole -- they probably had several mikes on the stage, you know, so it would pick up just about anything and everything.

That was my main interest, was the bass fiddle.
